item.title: “Great king, there are three things in the world which, when they arise, lead to harm, suffering, and discomfort. What three? Great king, greed is…
item.description:
“Great king, there are three things in the world which, when they arise, lead to harm, suffering, and discomfort. What three? Great king, greed is a thing in the world which, when it arises, leads to harm, suffering, and discomfort. Great king, hatred is a thing in the world which, when it arises, leads to harm, suffering, and discomfort. Great king, delusion is a thing in the world which, when it arises, leads to harm, suffering, and discomfort. These three things in the world, when they arise, bring harm, suffering, and discomfort.

Greed, hatred, delusion — these three,
Are evil minds for a person,
They damage one’s own self,
They produce one’s own self,
Like the rind and core of a tree,
Producing its own fruit.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 3.23

item.title: Then Māra, having transformed himself into a brahmin with a large topknot, wearing an antelope skin, old, bent like a rafter, breathing heavily, carrying a…
item.description:
Then Māra, having transformed himself into a brahmin with a large topknot, wearing an antelope skin, old, bent like a rafter, breathing heavily, carrying a udumbara staff, approached those monks. Having approached, he said to them:
- “Venerable sirs, you have gone forth too young, in the prime of youth, with black hair, in the bloom of youth, at the early stage of life, without having enjoyed sensual pleasures. Venerable sirs, enjoy human sensual pleasures. Do not abandon the present to chase after what is subject to time.”

- “Brahmin, we do not abandon the present to chase after what is subject to time. And, brahmin, we abandon what is subject to time to chase after the present. The Blessed One has said that sensual pleasures are subject to time, of great suffering, of great despair — the peril in them is even greater. This Dhamma is visible here and now, not subject to time, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 4.21

item.title: “Through lust for form, monks, consciousness becomes established with a foothold. With form as its object, with form as its support, seeking delight, it grows,…
item.description:
“Through lust for form, monks, consciousness becomes established with a foothold. With form as its object, with form as its support, seeking delight, it grows, increases, and expands. Through lust for feeling … for perception … for formations, monks, consciousness becomes established with a foothold. With formations as its object, with formations as its support, seeking delight, it grows, increases, and expands. Monks, if anyone says: ‘Apart from form, apart from feeling, apart from perception, apart from formations, I will show the coming and going, the passing away and arising, the growth, increase, and expansion of consciousness’ — such a thing is not possible. Monks, if a monk has abandoned lust for the form element — with the abandonment of lust, the basis is cut off, the support of consciousness does not exist. Monks, if he has abandoned lust for the feeling element … for the perception element … for the formation element … for the consciousness element — with the abandonment of lust, the basis is cut off, the support of consciousness does not exist. Without that support, consciousness does not expand, does not generate activity, and is liberated; being liberated, it is steady; being steady, it is content; being content, it is not agitated; being not agitated, he personally attains Nibbāna. He knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.54

item.title: Bemused by wealth and sensual pleasures, People are greedy and deluded, In the midst of sensual pleasures, Without clear awareness, They are overly intoxicated, Like…
item.description:
Bemused by wealth and sensual pleasures,
People are greedy and deluded,
In the midst of sensual pleasures,
Without clear awareness,
They are overly intoxicated,
Like a fish unaware of the trap set —
Later they suffer,
Experiencing the results of evil deeds.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 3.7

item.title: Elder Māluṅkyaputta: Seeing a form, mindfulness is lost — If one attends to a pleasing perception, The mind feels infatuation, Gets stuck and remains. His…
item.description:
Elder Māluṅkyaputta:

Seeing a form, mindfulness is lost —
If one attends to a pleasing perception,
The mind feels infatuation,
Gets stuck and remains.

His feelings increase,
Manyfold, born from form —
Greed and harmful thoughts grow strong,
They afflict his mind.
Suffering accumulates thus —
Far, far away is Nibbāna.

Hearing a sound, mindfulness is lost —
If one attends to a pleasing perception,
The mind feels infatuation,
Gets stuck and remains.

His feelings increase,
Manyfold, born from sound —
Greed and harmful thoughts grow strong,
They afflict his mind.
Suffering accumulates thus —
Far, far away is Nibbāna.

Smelling an odor, mindfulness is lost —
If one attends to a pleasing perception,
The mind feels infatuation,
Gets stuck and remains.

His feelings increase,
Manyfold, born from odor —
Greed and harmful thoughts grow strong,
They afflict his mind.
Suffering accumulates thus —
Far, far away is Nibbāna.

Tasting a flavor, mindfulness is lost —
If one attends to a pleasing perception,
The mind feels infatuation,
Gets stuck and remains.

His feelings increase,
Manyfold, born from taste —
Greed and harmful thoughts grow strong,
They afflict his mind.
Suffering accumulates thus —
Far, far away is Nibbāna.

Feeling a touch, mindfulness is lost —
If one attends to a pleasing perception,
The mind feels infatuation,
Gets stuck and remains.

His feelings increase,
Manyfold, born from touch —
Greed and harmful thoughts grow strong,
They afflict his mind.
Suffering accumulates thus —
Far, far away is Nibbāna.

Cognizing a phenomenon, mindfulness is lost —
If one attends to a pleasing perception,
The mind feels infatuation,
Gets stuck and remains.

His feelings increase,
Manyfold, born from mind —
Greed and harmful thoughts grow strong,
They afflict his mind.
Suffering accumulates thus —
Far, far away is Nibbāna.

From: Theragāthā 16.5

item.title: “Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, but still has a tendency towards something, that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness.…
item.description:
“Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, but still has a tendency towards something, that becomes a basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is a basis, there is an establishment of consciousness. When consciousness is established and grows, there is a production of future renewed existence. When there is future renewed existence, future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise. Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.38

item.title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline, as great desire. For one with…
item.description:
“I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline, as great desire. For one with great desire, monks, unarisen unwholesome states arise and arisen wholesome states decline.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.62

item.title: “Furthermore, monks, one sees that woman’s corpse thrown in a charnel ground — with skeleton still connected, still having flesh and blood, held together by…
item.description:
“Furthermore, monks, one sees that woman’s corpse thrown in a charnel ground — with skeleton still connected, still having flesh and blood, held together by sinews … with skeleton still connected, without flesh but smeared with blood, held together by sinews … without flesh, without blood, held together by sinews … disconnected bones scattered here and there — here a hand bone, here a foot bone, here a shin bone, here a thigh bone, here a hip bone, here a back bone, here a skull. What do you think, monks? Has her former charm and beauty disappeared and peril become evident?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Thus, monks, is the peril in the case of forms.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 13 – Mahādukkhakkhandhasutta

item.title: “Sunakkhatta, I give this simile to make the meaning clear. The meaning here is this: The wound, Sunakkhatta, is a synonym for the six sense-bases…
item.description:
“Sunakkhatta, I give this simile to make the meaning clear. The meaning here is this: The wound, Sunakkhatta, is a synonym for the six sense-bases (phassayatana). The poison, Sunakkhatta, is a synonym for ignorance. The dart, Sunakkhatta, is a synonym for craving. The probing tool, Sunakkhatta, is a synonym for mindfulness. The knife, Sunakkhatta, is a synonym for noble wisdom. The surgeon, Sunakkhatta, is a synonym for the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Indeed, Sunakkhatta, a monk who guards himself in regard to the six sense-bases, knowing that ‘Attachment (upadhi) is the root of suffering,’ becomes unattached and liberated by the destruction of attachment. It does not happen that he would still focus his body on attachment or direct his mind to attachment.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 105 – Sunakkhattasutta
